summary:
The most terrible thing has happened: we moved to a new apartment and I lost the copy of Limbo that had that picture of that girl that I liked so much. I’ve spent the entire day today going through every closet and drawer and box of docu­ ments and it is gone. Could you send me another? And you wrote me a real nice note on July 5 saying you’d found her and described her thus: “She speaks English, she’s a student, she is red-headed,” so I guess you can tell by this description which girl I mean. You also said you would be able to send me enlargements of pictures of her in “about three weeks,” but golly, Jannick, this is September and every day I stand outside by the mailbox, except for Sunday, and no pictures of her show up. This is not to upbraid you, but only to beg, to plead ... I just learned toward that United Artists is having DO ANDROIDS DREAM OF ELECTRIC SHEEP? read with the idea of making it into a movie. And luck is with me: I know the chick who is reading it for them, and I know that she thinks it is a great book. So even if this red-haired girl can’t act you might men­ tion it to her, because there is a big role in that for a chick, the part of Rachael 
Rosen. Originally, when a small independent company was interested in it for a movie, I had a rock critic friend give a copy of the book to Gracie Slick to read, with the idea of her doing that part. We now have a little new baby, Christopher, and he is very serious and never ceases to scowl. Doubleday will be bring...
